prep.summary: Your meetings from the past two days—the ATS Town Hall on September 2 and ATS Problem Solving on September 1—reveal a rapid centralization of technology governance. You are transitioning from line-of-business software silos to unified enterprise capability platforms—enforced by mandatory Architecture Intake Assessments integrated directly into the contract procurement workflow. Additionally, the cloud strategy has officially pivoted to an all-in AWS model—forcing an immediate exit of GCP workloads over to AWS Bedrock.
tasks: Establish the mandatory checkpoints for the Architecture Intake Assessment within the Contract Lifecycle Management system to prevent unapproved software purchases.
Map the Total Cost of Ownership across all capability platforms—prioritizing Build the Business by month-end—to identify and eliminate redundant software.
Execute the migration of all GCP workloads—specifically Vertex AI and Gemini models—to AWS Bedrock to align with the native AWS resiliency mandate.
Deploy the newly adopted BPM+ standard for business process orchestration across all enterprise workflow systems.
prep.title: ATS Leaderhip

events.summary: Check decisions ready for final review.

prep.summary: You must resolve the conflict over the failed policy summary database—which Aaron's team wants to abandon despite five years of stable usage in Auto. You also need to manage the integration of the newly finalized second investigation vendor—onboarded to handle automated referrals from PWC Risk Detect—while operational workflows remain manual. Focus your review on challenging the policy architects and examining the finalized decision artifacts.
tasks: Challenge the policy architects regarding the reliability and long-term status of the Kafka-sourced policy summary database.
Examine the finalized decision artifacts and documentation stored from the SIU TD meeting.
Monitor the manual portal workflows for the new investigation vendor to prevent bottlenecks from the expected PWC Risk Detect referral uptick.
prep.title: Check decisions ready for final review.

prep.summary: During your last meeting on July 20, you discussed major leadership changes at USAA—specifically the departures of Jeff Kalyazinski and Deepak Shimaro—alongside a strategic shift toward a "Best of Suite" tooling model. You reviewed operational recovery efforts after a massive 3,000-change system deployment caused outages, highlighting Randy's push for stronger diagnostic tools to protect core user flows. Finally, you evaluated the telematics strategy—shifting focus from mobile-device CMT data to direct OEM integrations with Toyota, Stellantis, and Ford.
tasks: Confirm the organizational footprint of RV—the new leader who started orientation on July 20—following the departures of Kalyazinski and Shimaro.
Assess the deployment of Randy's proposed diagnostic tools—intended to stabilize core systems—after the recent production outages.
Review the transition from CMT telematics to direct OEM data partnerships—specifically Toyota, Stellantis, and Ford—to eliminate third-party fees.
Verify the development status of Leapfrog—noting whether it remains reliant on mobile CMT data or has transitioned to native vehicle usage features.
prep.title: Bi-monthly sync with Ryan Rist

prep.summary: Examine the consolidated platform hierarchy from the August 31 session—you must align with the collapse of standalone Web and Mobile categories under Member Digital. Complete the outstanding Level 3 capability mappings—this prevents double-counting during your financial roll-ups. Apply the TIME lifecycle metadata to your target architectures—this will automate your roadmap and Gantt chart generation.
tasks: Finalize Level 1 and Level 2 capability mappings in the central workspace spreadsheet.
Resolve duplicate mappings across Level 2 categories to prevent double-counting of infrastructure costs.
Incorporate the TIME model lifecycle metadata and UUIDs into the mapping database.
Assess the proposed "Legacy Tax" framework to incentivize line-of-business migrations.
prep.title: Platform strategy
